newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan sets November date for national elections.
newsitem.headline: Jordan sets November date for national elections.

text.p: Jordan's cabinet on Tuesday said parliamentary elections would be held in the kingdom in early November , the official Petra news agency reported.

The agency said Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali's cabinet decided to set November 4, 1997 as the date of elections which King Hussein last month ordered the government to formally prepare to hold later in the year.

Elections were due within four years of last elections in November 1993 which is the standard parliamentary term but according to the constitution King Hussein could have extended the existing parliament if he wished.

The influential Moslem Brotherhood followed by their political arm the Islamic Action Front (IAF) have already called for a boycott of the polls, complaining that parliament has been sidelined in the four years since the last elections.

The remaining left-wing and pan Arab opposition parties are nearly evenly split between following suit and a conditional participation in the elections if the government freezes implementing a tough press law and pledges to end curbs on public freedoms.
